solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One churchman or another entertaining company

indicators.note: to entertain is to have a guest within, so one churchman's title takes the firm inside it

parts.note: another churchman: a dean heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: Talk of clergy, one of them hosting a business group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or another' makes the clue look like a choice between two clerics; in fact the second churchman is the container and the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest, so one kind of churchman.

clue.text: Blue feathers spread out

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers
to cast is to throw or scatter widely, spread out

explanation.surface: A bird with blue plumage fanned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour for the feathers; it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means low in spirits, so dejected and downcast.

clue.text: AA named us in error time after time

indicators.note: something in error is wrong, so the letters must be put right by rearranging

explanation.surface: The motoring organisation keeps getting our name wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam means repeatedly to a tiresome degree, over and over again.

clue.text: Round 10: greatest boxer first to succumb in plant

parts.note: O is a round shape
X is the Roman numeral for ten
Muhammad Ali called himself 'the greatest'

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Boxing commentary: in round ten the greatest fighter is the first to go down.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxalis, or wood sorrel, is a genus of flowering plants with clover-like leaves.

clue.text: Old Asian man, not the Messiah, outside a court

indicators.note: the man's name stands outside, wrapping round the article and the court

parts.note: from the Monty Python film Life of Brian: 'He's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy'

explanation.surface: Describing an ancient man of Asia, who is pointedly not the saviour, standing outside a court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Messiah line is a Monty Python joke: in Life of Brian, Brian's mother insists he is not the Messiah.
explanation.definitionFit: Bactria was an ancient region of central Asia, so a Bactrian is an inhabitant of it from antiquity.

clue.text: Three stars from Catharine cavorting with Paul

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about, so the names' letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Three celebrities emerge from a couple, Catharine and Paul, frolicking together.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is a triple star system, the nearest to the Sun.

clue.text: Merry monarch gets closer

parts.note: merry and tight are both slang for drunk
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A cheerful king grows more intimate with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry monarch' suggests Charles II, nicknamed the Merry Monarch, but the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Tighter means more closely fitted or packed, nearer together.

clue.text: Senseless China News content

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Criticism of the meaningless content of a Chinese news service.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense.

clue.text: Kind disposition

definitions.meaning: a sort or type, as in things of this kind

explanation.surface: A gentle temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature means a sort or class of thing, and also a person's inborn character.

clue.text: Cash in silver immediately withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
now means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: Money held as silver is suddenly taken out of the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' suits the banking surface but signals reading AGNOW backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonga is British slang for money, a casual synonym for cash.

clue.text: Abhorrent ruling to imprison reversed before magistrates

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the word for ruling encloses the other piece

parts.note: regnant means reigning, currently ruling

indicators.note: reversed tells us to turn the short word backwards

parts.note: to be up before the magistrates is to be in court, so this is up

explanation.surface: A court decision so loathsome it is overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British idiom, someone 'up before the magistrates' is appearing in court, so 'before magistrates' stands for the little word that 'reversed' then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means causing strong disgust, a direct synonym for abhorrent.

clue.text: Wave coming over ship makes for thrilling ride

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece coming over the other sits above it

parts.note: a roller is a long swelling wave
a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: A wave breaking over a ship gives the crew an exciting ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster is a fairground ride with steep drops and fast turns.

clue.text: Important old Irish police independent in state

indicators.note: in places the police and independent within the abbreviation of the state

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001

explanation.surface: A notable former Irish police officer working alone in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucial means decisive or critical, so of great importance.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature has an illness, needing attention

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis, an illness
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A night animal is sick and needs looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: The antbear, or aardvark, is an African mammal that feeds by night on ants and termites.

clue.text: Shack in Slough

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A hut in the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town west of London; it is the verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple hut, and to shed skin is to slough it.

clue.text: Cars here to be broken in systematic investigation

indicators.note: broken things are smashed into new pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cars are to be wrecked here as part of a scientific study.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is careful methodical study to establish facts.

clue.text: Disorganised leader to host a quiet venture

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
to hazard is to venture or risk

explanation.surface: A chaotic leader is about to host a low-key enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means lacking order or plan, random.

clue.text: Ancestor warning creature in woods

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn of a ball coming
a bear is an animal of the forest

explanation.surface: A forefather warns of a beast in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Treat cold when brought in to liaise

indicators.note: being brought in means entering, so the letter goes inside the verb

parts.note: to mediate is to act as go-between, to liaise between parties
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A doctor's cold remedy, delivered once go-betweens are called in.
explanation.definitionFit: To medicate is to give drugs to a patient, to treat them.

clue.text: Intelligent swimmer working on DPhil

indicators.note: working means being processed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A clever athlete swimmer studying for a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: DPhil is the Oxford name for a doctorate, which suits 'intelligent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dolphin is a marine mammal famed for its intelligence.

clue.text: Surgery — evidently reversible — seen in China

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

indicators.note: a reversible thing can be turned round, so the same short word follows backwards

explanation.surface: An operation that can be undone, performed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is rhyming slang: 'china plate' means mate. The answer reads the same either way, which is what 'evidently reversible' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a close friend or colleague, as china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang.

clue.text: Goddess making appearance after credit crunch

indicators.note: after places the goddess behind the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Isis was an Egyptian goddess

explanation.surface: A deity appears in the wake of the credit crunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit crunch' reads as one phrase; 'crunch' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a critical moment or emergency, as in when it comes to the crunch.

clue.text: Alumnus, boring perhaps, certainly not square

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
long can mean tediously lengthy, so boring

explanation.surface: A former student, dull maybe, but definitely not old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like slang for unfashionable; it is the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle with unequal sides, so its shape is not square.

clue.text: A1 drink knocked back in Crown & Sceptre

indicators.note: drinks knocked back are downed, but here the letters are sent back to front

parts.note: A1 is read as the letters A and I, the figure 1 standing for I
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A first-rate pint downed in a pub called the Crown & Sceptre.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown & Sceptre looks like a pub name; it is the definition, as royal insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty, such as the crown and sceptre.

clue.text: Sauce from elegist penning verse

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the poet's name holds the letter

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A sauce from a poet of elegies who has written a verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is a sauce made from meat juices.

clue.text: Universal anger about doctor's offence

indicators.note: about here means coming round to follow, so the anger is placed after the doctor

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Everyone is furious about something a doctor did.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so umbrage is a feeling of resentment.

clue.text: Get this cooked before old man comes in for food

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the father goes inside the scrambled letters
cooked figures are falsified, rearranged, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: old man is a colloquial term for father, pa

explanation.surface: Instructions to get a meal cooked before father comes home for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns GET THIS into SGHETTI; 'comes in' puts PA inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, a staple food.

clue.text: Give speech from floor at eleven

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone takes the floor to speak at eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech.

clue.text: Perhaps beside a river, a vale to the east?

parts.note: say means for example, perhaps
on can mean beside, as in a town on a river

explanation.surface: A scenic description: maybe beside a river, a valley to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vale' is not a valley but the Latin word for farewell; 'to the east' points to Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayonara is the Japanese goodbye, an Eastern equivalent of the Latin farewell 'vale'.

clue.text: Wander in breeze in Moroccan seaport

indicators.note: in places the wandering word inside the breeze

parts.note: air can mean a light breeze
to gad about is to wander around

explanation.surface: Strolling in the sea breeze of a Moroccan port.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city on Morocco's Atlantic coast.
